title: Nepal Earthquake | Tech Support From Google, Facebook, Viber
description: The worst earthquake to have struck Nepal in 8 decades has caused wide spread devastation in the Himalayan nation. But amidst all the damage in Nepal, rescue operations are relying on technology. Google has activated the "people finder" platform, Facebook has launched a safety "check-in" feature and apps like Viber, Skype and telcos like Bharti Airtel are offering free or cheaper calls to and from Nepal! asr.full_text: Seventy-two hours after a series of earthquakes shattered Nepal and parts of India, rescue teams are still looking for clues, even after recovering over 3,200 bodies. The killer tremors have thrown communication links out of gear. Internet access has been restricted, while mobile phone connectivity is unreliable. Apart from the mammoth rehabilitation efforts, re-establishing communication links have emerged as a top priority area. Internet search giant Google has activated the Peoplegender platform which allows users to post and search for information about missing friends and relatives and as of now it is tracking over 5,000 records. Google had created this feature in response to the destructive 2010 earthquake in Haiti! Google is also reducing the cost of calls made to Nepal through its Google Voice service from 19 Cents a minute to 1 Cent a minute. While Facebook has started the Safety Check-In feature, which allows users in affected areas to select a notification alerting friends on their network that they are safe. popular voice and messaging app vibe that has over 3 million users in the himalayan kingdom has turned off billing for users in nepal to landlines or mobile phones globally. meanwhile in India bhakthi airtel has offered free calls to Nepal for the next 30 hours, IDea has slashed STD rates to Nepal from 12 rupees per minute to one rupee per minute. BSNL & MTNL are also offering calls to Nepal at local rates. With Nitya Balakrishnan, Krishna Kumar, ETnow, Mumbai.
